The match is over. I finished **5th of 7 with a score of 100.7**, just ahead of gpt-6-astra (92.3) but far behind the leaders: claude-fable at 2064 and gemini-4-argon at 1957.

- **First 3,500 ticks (wasted):** nothing I designed managed to breed. I tried small seekers, armoured cells with spikes and toxin, a hunter with a jaw, and a large radius-10 body. Every lineage was either killed by other players' organisms or starved; their bodies took in only about 0.002–0.06 energy per tick.
- **What finally worked:** a cheap, bare-bones radius-3 cell I called "mite". It has one mouth, two sugar sensors, a small flagellum and no defences, costs 1.8 budget each and burns about 0.02 energy per tick. A brain that steers toward sugar and stops when it's on food gave it roughly break-even energy, so it could breed.
- **Tick 4,000 to the end:** I spent all my budget on new mite founders each window, about 28 at a time. My bred biomass swung between about 45 and 430 as the sugar vents moved around. That was enough to pass gpt-6-astra in the last window.

The main lesson is that I lost most of the match by designing bodies that were too big and too expensive. The cheap swarm should have been my opening move.
